big_picture_notes: Jude is a tightly constructed, single‑chapter polemical letter in classic Hellenistic form (salutation 1–2; body 3–23; doxology 24–25). Structural cohesion comes from pervasive triplets (hendiatris), aggressive historical typology (Israel/angels/Sodom; Cain/Balaam/Korah), and an inclusio of ‘kept’/‘keeping’ (1, 21, 24). The narrative arc moves from intended topic → urgent call to contend (3–4) → proof of certain judgment for intruders (5–16) → final exhortations to the faithful (17–23), concluding with a preservation‑focused doxology.

stories.story_title: The Call to Contend and the Doom of the Godless
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Start (1:1) epistolary opening marks the beginning; end (1:25) doxology completes the letter. Glue: recurring triplets, historical typology proving judgment, and ‘kept/keep’ inclusio framing the call to contend and God’s preserving power.

scenes.scene_name: Salutation and the Call to Contend
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Jude greets the called and beloved, urging them to contend for the faith against intruders marked for condemnation.
Unbelieving Israel, the fallen angels, and Sodom — three proofs that God judges the ungodly.
The false teachers defile and revile, unlike even Michael, who left judgment to the Lord.
Cain, Balaam, and Korah; hidden reefs, waterless clouds, fruitless trees, wandering stars.
The seventh from Adam foretold the Lord's coming judgment on these discontented flatterers.

scenes.scene_name: Remember the Apostles' Warning of Scoffers
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The foretold last-times scoffers, worldly and devoid of the Spirit, who cause divisions.

scenes.scene_name: Build Yourselves Up and Snatch Others from the Fire
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Keep in God's love; have mercy on doubters and rescue others, hating the flesh-stained garment.
To Him able to keep them from stumbling — glory, majesty, dominion, and authority forever.
